indicators.note: whatever breaks is smashed apart, so the letters of the possessive phrase after it are shattered and reassembled

parts.note: the letters of these words, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Some fixture in Parliament defies a rule named after a Mr Cook.
explanation.walkthrough: The WOOLSACK is the wool-stuffed seat of the Lord Speaker in the House of Lords.
explanation.definitionFit: The wool-stuffed cushion seat has stood permanently in the House of Lords chamber for centuries, a fixed piece of its furniture.

clue.text: Nobel laureate made TV appearance — about time!

indicators.note: the phrase goes around the letter for time

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A prize-winner finally appeared on television.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About time!' reads as an exclamation of impatience but holds the container and its filling.
explanation.definitionFit: James Watson shared the 1962 Nobel Prize for discovering the double-helix structure of DNA.

clue.text: Twist at start of lively dance for a very large number

indicators.note: twisting the opening turns its first two letters the other way round

explanation.surface: A twirl that opens a spirited ballroom dance.
explanation.definitionFit: An octillion is ten to the power twenty-seven in the short scale, an enormous figure.

clue.text: Amazing ball that has to be signed for

definitions.text: that has to be signed for

explanation.surface: A cricket bowler's wonder ball earns a mark of approval.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a delivery is a single ball bowled. Special Delivery is a Royal Mail guaranteed next-day service needing a signature.
explanation.definitionFit: A guaranteed postal service in Britain requires the recipient to sign on receipt of the item.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a baked fruit pudding with a scone topping
second meaning: someone who mends shoes

explanation.definitionFit: One word names both a fruit pudding topped with biscuit dough and a tradesman who repairs footwear.

clue.text: Comes out as terrorist group takes legal action

parts.note: IS is the abbreviation for Islamic State

explanation.surface: Something emerges while a terrorist group goes to court.
explanation.definitionFit: A publication or statement that issues is released or emerges, the same verb sense as coming out.

clue.text: Player is younger after makeover, partners say

indicators.note: a makeover remodels appearance, so the preceding letters are given a new arrangement

parts.note: the letters of these two words
a couple refer to themselves together as we

explanation.surface: A couple claim an actor looks younger after a cosmetic makeover.
explanation.definitionFit: Sigourney Weaver is the American actress who starred in Alien, and an actor is a player on stage or screen.

explanation.surface: A delivery firm in difficulties is being filmed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone upset is distressed or worried, an adjective that matches being troubled.

indicators.note: without a tail means the final letter of the meat is cut off

explanation.surface: Someone grabs meat and a fish with no tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tailless' seems to describe the fish but docks the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealing is the act of taking something without permission, a gerund matching the participle taking.

indicators.note: the numeral departs from the following word, so it is removed

explanation.surface: Someone drops off a bouquet on the stages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like plant foliage beside flowers, but it is a verb: the I departs from DAISIES.
explanation.definitionFit: A dais is a raised stage at one end of a hall for speakers or dignitaries.

indicators.note: says the letters sit inside the run of words that follows, spanning the word breaks

parts.note: the end of the country, the whole of the pronoun and the start of the verb

explanation.surface: A statement about property law in Egypt.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal title is the right of ownership of property, as in holding title to land or a car.

clue.text: A massive Cockney in top European film

indicators.note: the phrase before it is placed inside the word for top

parts.note: E is the standard abbreviation for European

indicators.note: a Cockney speaker drops the initial h, so the adjective before it loses its first letter

explanation.surface: Praise for a huge, London-accented European film at the top of its class.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys famously drop their aitches, so 'Cockney' trims the h from the word for massive. 'Top' reads as an adjective for the film but is the outer word.
explanation.definitionFit: Beau Geste is the 1939 Foreign Legion adventure film with Gary Cooper, adapted from the P C Wren novel.

clue.text: Irritated, so I filled areas drilled

indicators.note: something irritated is stirred up and agitated, so the following letters are jumbled

parts.note: the letters of these three words

explanation.surface: An annoyed worker grumbles about having had to backfill the drilled areas.
explanation.definitionFit: Oil companies sink wells into these petroleum-bearing tracts of land or seabed, so they are places that get bored.

indicators.note: something returned comes back the way it went, so the combined letters read in the opposite direction

parts.note: the thirteenth letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A tipsy Greek man came back home in the past.
explanation.definitionFit: Both work as conjunctions of time: wait until dawn and do not leave before dawn mean the same.

clue.text: Playwright's mother beginning to getting less healthy

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, so only the opening of mother is kept

explanation.surface: A dramatist's mother has begun to decline in health.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's reads as 'is': the playwright is M followed by ILLER.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Miller wrote Death of a Salesman and The Crucible, so he is a famous dramatist.

clue.text: Star — which this isn't, at the end of the day

parts.note: this clue is an across clue, so it is not a down clue

explanation.surface: A celebrity is described as something that this is not, when all is said and done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This' is the clue itself: it sits among the across clues, so it isn't DOWN. 'At the end of the day' looks like a cliché but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sundown is sunset, the evening moment when daylight finishes and night begins.

parts.note: as in a sight better, a great deal

explanation.surface: A bargain from the past turns out to have been an error.
explanation.definitionFit: An oversight is an unintentional failure to notice something, a lapse or slip.

indicators.note: the second word sits inside the name of the god

explanation.surface: The Greek war deity phoned in his commands.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrange things is to put them in sequence, and to order them is the same verb sense.

parts.note: R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Opposition stirs up fury among football players.
explanation.walkthrough: Rangers is a Glasgow football club; QPR in London are also known as Rangers.
explanation.definitionFit: Rangers is a Scottish professional soccer club, so its players can be called by that team name.

indicators.note: agents who infiltrate get inside, so the spies go into the star

explanation.surface: Secret agents gatecrash a celebrity's bash.
explanation.definitionFit: A social is an informal gathering or get-together, often held by a club or church.

explanation.surface: An animal shelter that was the first of its kind was purpose-built.
explanation.definitionFit: Something styled has been given a deliberate shape or fashion by a designer, as with hair or a dress.

parts.note: the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: An engineer's meaning is being explained.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who means what they say is genuine and honest in feeling, so they are sincere.

parts.note: surface reading: Dr Watson was a dull companion
setter's reading: the sidekick is a doctor, which opens the answer with DR, and he tells every tale at length

explanation.walkthrough: Dr Watson narrates the Holmes stories at length, so the sidekick talked on and on; the answer opens with DR, his title. The wordplay beyond that is not clear-cut.
explanation.definitionFit: To drone is to speak in a dull monotonous tone, so someone who droned was tedious to listen to.

clue.text: Very musical association with computer thinking

parts.note: ASS is a standard abbreviation for association

explanation.surface: A tuneful society meets machine intelligence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very musical' reads like praise; it means the word for very in musical directions.
explanation.definitionFit: Assai is an Italian term in score markings, as in allegro assai, meaning extremely or quite.

clue.text: Scientists apparently now expect Republican leaders to be comparatively rational

indicators.note: the leaders of words are their first letters, the ones at the front

parts.note: the initials of these five words

explanation.surface: A prediction that Republican leaders will become more reasonable.
explanation.definitionFit: Saner is the comparative of sane, describing someone more level-headed and reasonable than another.

clue.text: Being in credit, Danish city acquires new electrical component

indicators.note: says what follows ends up sitting inside the abbreviation for credit
the city takes the next letter into itself, so it goes inside

parts.note: a city on Funen, birthplace of Hans Christian Andersen
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A Danish city has acquired a new component and its finances are healthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being in credit' sounds like solvency, but it says the rest goes inside the abbreviation. Odense is Denmark's third-largest city, birthplace of Hans Christian Andersen.
explanation.definitionFit: A condenser is the older name for a capacitor, a circuit part that stores electric charge.

indicators.note: the letters are taken out from within the run of words that follows

parts.note: the tail of the first word, the middle word and the start of the last

explanation.surface: After Prohibition, a drink once smuggled became legal.
explanation.definitionFit: A fizzy soft beverage flavoured with ginger root, often used as a mixer.

clue.text: Strict sort of diet for one in the lead

indicators.note: the abbreviation before it sits inside the word for the lead

parts.note: the van is the front, the vanguard

explanation.surface: A particular diet is the front-runner.
explanation.definitionFit: A vegan regime avoids all animal products, eggs and dairy included, so it is a rigorous form of vegetarianism.

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for saint

explanation.surface: A holy person requests some bouquets.
explanation.definitionFit: A spray is a small bunch of flowers or a single branch with blossoms, used as a decoration or corsage.

clue.text: Second journalist covering island gets hidden away

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second

indicators.note: the second and the journalist wrap round the island, which sits inside

explanation.surface: A second reporter covers a story on an island and is spirited away.
explanation.definitionFit: To secrete something is to conceal it somewhere private, so a thing secreted has been stashed out of sight.
